title: Evolution candidate
description: A proposed change to an evolvable harness artifact, with its lineage and every evaluation stage. A candidate missing a stage cannot be promoted; that is enforced rather than documented.

kind.description: What Evolution.propose_from_cluster/1 writes (signals, capability, gates_policy, skill) as well as the older hand-proposed kinds. constitution, trust, gate, security and policy are here because proposing a change to them is allowed and landing one never is (Evolution.protected_target?/1, constitution §4); a schema that refused them would stop the proposal the harness wants to be able to make.

weakness.description: A task family, observed in telemetry. Not an anecdote.

disconfirming_evidence.description: What result would tell you this is wrong.

stages.description: Each stage is absent until run. Promotion requires all of sandbox, benchmark, holdout, transfer, anti_goodhart and archive.

fitness.description: A vector, deliberately. A single scalar is something to optimise, and something will optimise it.

metrics.description: Declared at proposal and frozen there. `record_stage/3` refuses to change them: metrics an optimising agent can edit are metrics an optimising agent will edit, and the edit arrives looking like a result.

capability.description: What must not get worse, and by how much it may move first.

fitness_provenance.description: Where each set-keyed fitness value came from, keyed by set name. A number typed on a command line and a number produced by running a candidate against the suite are indistinguishable in the file; this is what tells them apart, and `promotable?/1` refuses a set-keyed value without it.

run.description: The run ledger id of the scoring run. Something to go and read.

environments.description: The environment ids actually scored. Checked against the set's currently verified members: a member that has since stopped verifying, or one added since, makes the number about a different suite.

scored_by.description: The adapter and model the scoring run used.

application.description: How to make this candidate present in a working tree. `target` names what the candidate is about; this is what a scoring run checks out. Only `git_ref` can be run: a commit either exists or it does not, where a JSON field an agent can write means nothing.

baseline.description: The commit it is measured against. Both arms run the same environments; the fitness value is the difference in solve rate.

run.description: The run this candidate was proposed in. It is taken from the ledger when the proposer is in a run, and it can also be supplied. A held-out measurement produced by this run, or by anything it dispatched, is refused. Both ids must name runs that exist, so a candidate claiming to have been proposed elsewhere has to name a run the ledger records — which makes a forgery a trace rather than an unfalsifiable claim. It does not prove who ran what; a signature does that.

independent.description: True when the runner is not the candidate's author. Required true for holdout and anti_goodhart.
